method.summary: 35 real trade-business homepages (US 24, AU 5, UK 3, CA 3) across all 10 trades were fetched and audited for the same checklist: header, hero copy, CTAs, emergency/response claims, offers, pricing, trust signals, form fields, service area, booking, photos. A further 9 sites were reviewed but left out of `sites` because they were weak; they are used only as evidence in `anti_patterns` (see `reviewed_not_listed`). Third-party feature counts from Colorlib's audited roundups (plumbing 18, HVAC 30, roofing 27, electrical 19, painting 23, pest 23, cleaning 26 sites) are used to cross-check prevalence.
method.prevalence_denominator: Unless stated otherwise, 'N/35' counts the 35 sites in `sites`. Trade subsets: roofing 7 (incl. Puetz), HVAC/heating 7 (incl. multi-trade Hiller, Snell, Fallon, Service Today, BOXT), plumbing-led 5 (Superior, Pimlico, Aspect, Fallon, Service Today), electrical 3, pest 3, cleaning 2, painting 2, remodeling 3, garage doors 2, landscaping 4.
method.limits: Pages were read as extracted text, not rendered. Sticky/fixed bars, map embeds, page speed and visual layout are therefore under-counted or unmeasured; photo authenticity was judged from alt text and filenames. Prevalence for those patterns is a lower bound.

conversion_patterns.name: Every phone number is a tap-to-call link
conversion_patterns.what: Every printed number is an <a href="tel:+1XXXXXXXXXX"> link (E.164 in the href, local format in the text). Place it in the header, hero, after each service section and in the footer. Make the label an action, e.g. 'Call Now (843) 300-9675' or 'Call (206) 250-9193'. Use one number site-wide, or one per location.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 34/35 have tel: links somewhere (BOXT is the exception). Colorlib: tappable anywhere on 17/18 plumbing, 27/30 HVAC, 19/27 roofing and only 13/19 electrician sites.
conversion_patterns.evidence: https://colorlib.com/wp/plumbing-websites-design/ ; https://colorlib.com/wp/hvac-company-website-examples/ ; https://colorlib.com/wp/roofing-company-website-examples/ ; observed on Powerful Electrical, Hedlund Painting

conversion_patterns.name: Printed phone number in the header, with when it's answered
conversion_patterns.what: Top-right of the header on desktop, top bar on mobile. Print the digits (an icon alone doesn't count) and add a short line about availability: '24/7 Live Answering Service' (Smock), '24hrs & emergencies' (Pimlico), 'Call today for same day service' (Arrow), '7 Days 7AM TO 5PM' (Bright Electrical), 'Open Now' (Service Today). Multi-metro businesses list each metro number (Green Home Pest: Phoenix + Tucson; Garage Door Fix: Calgary + Edmonton + toll-free).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 31/35 print a tappable number in the header. Misses: Bumble, BOXT, Aspect (icon only), Neil Kelly. Colorlib: phone above the fold on 16/18 plumbing, 25/30 HVAC, 17/27 roofing, 10/19 electrician sites.
conversion_patterns.evidence: Smock HVAC, Pimlico Plumbers, Arrow Pest Control homepages; Colorlib counts above

conversion_patterns.name: Sticky call/quote bar on mobile
conversion_patterns.what: On mobile, a bar fixed to the bottom of the screen with 2 (at most 3) equal-width buttons: [Call] [Free Quote/Book], and optionally [Text]. At least 48px tall, with the safe-area inset. It stays visible while scrolling and hides while a form field has focus. Examples: Bone Dry 'CALL TODAY | 866.371.5090' + 'GET A FREE QUOTE'; Fallon phone + 'Book Online' + 'Text Us'; Nozzle Nolen 'Get My Free Quote' + 'Call Now'; A1 Garage 'Schedule Now'; Garage Door Fix floating 'Tap to call'.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: At least 7/35 visible in the page source (Bone Dry, Fallon, Nozzle Nolen, A1 Garage, Powerful Electrical, Garage Door Fix, Normandy's sticky header). This is a lower bound because pages were read as text. Also cited: A-1 Total Service Plumbing's 'fixed Call Now bar' (Colorlib), Retro Roofers' sticky header and MHI's floating review button (ServiceTitan), Jansen Roofing's sticky free-estimate tab (Hook Agency).

conversion_patterns.name: Two paths in the hero: quote/book plus call
conversion_patterns.what: The hero offers one main action (quote, book or estimate) and one secondary action that shows the phone number. Write the number into the secondary button and use soft wording for people who prefer to talk: 'Get Your Free Estimate' + 'Call (206) 250-9193' (Hedlund); 'Get a free quote' + 'Prefer to talk? (732) 536-6500' (Arrow); 'GET A QUOTE' + 'or call us on 1300 743 923' (DYAD); 'Schedule Now' + 'Call Now' (A1 Garage).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: About 11/35 have both actions in the hero itself (Hedlund, Snell, Arrow, DYAD, Powerful, Service Today, Fallon, A1 Garage, Garage Door Fix, Anderson, Pimlico). Unbounce: home-improvement pages offering mixed CTAs (click, form, phone) convert at 4% vs a 2.6% baseline.
conversion_patterns.evidence: https://unbounce.com/industry/home-improvement/ ; Arrow Pest Control, Hedlund Painting homepages

conversion_patterns.name: Emergency / 24-7 availability banner
conversion_patterns.what: Emergency trades get a top strip or header label that says when calls are answered and by whom: 'Call 843-300-9675, answered 24/7 by a real person' (Powerful); '24/7 availability on nights, weekends, and holidays at no extra cost' (Snell); 'for no heat furnace repair situations' (Ignite, seasonal). Only make the claim if a person really answers. Footer hours and the schema openingHoursSpecification must agree with it.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 14/35 overall. Plumbing/HVAC/multi-trade 9/10, roofing 2/7, electrical 1/3, garage doors 1/2. Colorlib: 16/18 plumbing, 24/30 HVAC, but only 5/19 electrician sites.

conversion_patterns.name: A response or arrival time the customer can check
conversion_patterns.what: Put a concrete, checkable time promise next to the CTA. Options: a cut-off rule ('If you book before midday, we guarantee a technician will be at your door that same day.' Service Today; 'Call before noon...' Arrow; 'Available when you call before noon' Nozzle Nolen); a measured rate ('over 96% of service calls on the same day'); an arrival courtesy call ('courtesy call 15-30 minutes before we arrive', Fallon); a booking lead time ('most appointments set within 24 hours', Tadlock); or a capped emergency target ('1-Hour Emergency Response Time*' with the caveat stated, Pimlico). Next to form submit buttons, say when you'll reply.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 11/35 make some same-day or response promise; 7/35 give a number or a cut-off time.

conversion_patterns.name: Name the free thing in the CTA
conversion_patterns.what: Put the free offer in the button text: 'Get My Free Estimate', 'Schedule Free Inspection', 'FREE 2nd Opinion on Major HVAC Repairs', 'FREE Electrical Panel Inspection', and add 'no obligation'. Painters and remodelers also say what the estimate excludes: 'a free written estimate with no surprise change orders' (Hedlund). When the job can be priced without a visit, skip the estimate and show the price instead (see price-transparency).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 21/35 overall; roofing 6/7 (Colorlib: free inspection on 19/27 roofing sites). Sites without it swap in published or instant pricing (BOXT, Tidy Casa, Maid Marines, Garage Door Fix, A1 estimator) or a disclosed call-out fee (Fallon).
conversion_patterns.evidence: https://colorlib.com/wp/roofing-company-website-examples/ ; Hedlund Painting, Smock HVAC, Powerful Electrical homepages

conversion_patterns.name: Show a 'from' price, a price model or a fee policy
conversion_patterns.what: Show at least one real number or explain how the work is priced. Options: a price list (Garage Door Fix: 'Starting at $380' springs, 'From $2,445' new door); a plan anchor ('plans start at $49 per month', Green Home Pest); an install anchor ('Installed from £1,890', BOXT); a worked invoice example (Hiller 'True Transparency Pricing'); a pricing model ('Set price jobs' / 'Half-hourly rate jobs' / 'Scoped jobs', Aspect); a disclosed call-out fee ('$88 call out fee', Fallon).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 17/35 show a number or an instant-price tool. The rest rely only on 'free estimate'.

conversion_patterns.name: Self-serve instant quote or estimator
conversion_patterns.what: A small estimator that returns a price or range before any contact details are asked for (ask for phone/email only to save or book). By trade: roofing = address + satellite measurement + material, returns a range ('Get instant quote and visualize your new roof', Bumble); water heater = tank/tankless + size ('INSTANT WATER HEATER QUOTE', Superior); HVAC replacement ('Instant HVAC Quote', Smock); cleaning = bedrooms/bathrooms/frequency to a flat rate (Tidy Casa, Maid Marines); remodeling cost calculators (Neil Kelly); garage door cost estimator ('No bait-and-switch. No pressure.', A1).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 10/35 (Bumble, Houston Roofing, Tadlock's '3-minute Roof Assessment', Smock, Superior, BOXT, Tidy Casa, Maid Marines, Neil Kelly, A1 Garage). Colorlib: Complete Climate Services and Superior Plumbing also offer instant quotes.

conversion_patterns.name: Financing shown as a monthly payment
conversion_patterns.what: Next to big-ticket services, show a monthly figure, the lender's name and a line saying checking won't affect credit: 'New HVAC System for as little as $113/month' (Snell); 'HVAC Systems Replacements Starting at $99/mo.' (Hiller); Tadlock's '$132/mo' example; 'with no impact to your credit score for checking options' (Guardian/Upgrade); '0% Interest payment plans available through Brighte' (Fallon). Put the APR and terms in small print.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 17/35 mention financing: roofing 6/7, HVAC/heating 7/7, remodeling 2/3. Only 4/35 show an actual monthly figure. Colorlib: roofing 12/27; HVAC 'pricing or financing' 23/30.

conversion_patterns.name: Named service area and a page per town
conversion_patterns.what: Name real towns on the homepage instead of 'and surrounding areas', grouped by sub-region when there are many (Hedlund: 'Seattle & North End', 'The Eastside'). Link each to a town page with local proof (projects, reviews and the crew from that town). Name the area in the H1 ('Heating & Cooling Services in Frederick & Montgomery County'). Keep the lists identical in the body, footer and schema areaServed.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 31/35 name their area (misses: BOXT, Bright, DYAD, Gibbs); about 20/35 link to town/county pages (Houston Roofing 33, Superior 29, Pimlico 32 boroughs). Colorlib: area named on 13/18 plumbing, 24/30 HVAC, 15/27 roofing, 10/19 electrician sites.
conversion_patterns.evidence: https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091 (relevance and distance drive local ranking) ; https://www.houstonroofingonline.com/ ; https://www.hedlundpainting.com/

conversion_patterns.name: Start with service + ZIP/postcode
conversion_patterns.what: Make the first step two fields: service and ZIP/postcode (or a city picker). Use them to route to the right branch, show local prices or availability, then ask for contact details. Examples: Aspect 'What do you need help with?' + 'Your postcode' then 'Check availability'; Garage Door Fix 'Find Your City' for 'local prices and a direct number'; Neil Kelly space + location; Benjamin Franklin Plumbing uses a ZIP box as its main CTA (Colorlib).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 7/35 (Aspect, Pimlico, Snell, Garage Door Fix, Bumble, Neil Kelly, A1 Garage).

conversion_patterns.name: Reviews with rating, count and source
conversion_patterns.what: Put an aggregate badge in the header or hero: stars + count + platform + a link to the profile ('4.9' / '335+ Google reviews' linked to Google Maps; 'Google rating 5.0 from 2,352 reviews'). Showing two or three platforms side by side is stronger (DYAD: Google, hipages, Facebook). Further down, show 3-6 recent reviews with first name, town, date and the job. Keep counts the same everywhere on the page and refresh them.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 12/35 show a rating or count with a named source; 21/35 show some aggregate; 14/35 show none (Snell, Hiller, Tadlock, Service Today, among others). BrightLocal 2026: 97% read reviews, 68% need 4+ stars, 47% won't use a business with under 20 reviews, 74% want reviews from the last 3 months.

conversion_patterns.name: Printed licence and insurance numbers
conversion_patterns.what: Print the licence number itself, not just 'Licensed & Insured': 'Lic. CCC1336800' (Tadlock), 'OR CCB #1663; WA L&I...' (Neil Kelly), 'QBCC Licence: 1304235', 'Licence EC11863' + 'ARC number' (Bright). Put it in the footer, near the quote form, and in a trust strip. Add 'bonded & insured' and a link to the certificate of insurance or WCB/workers' comp where relevant. In some places it's the law: California's CSLB requires the licence number in website ads (B&P 7030.5), and Queensland's QBCC requires name and licence number in website ads.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 12/35 print licence numbers; about 25/35 claim licensed/insured/accredited in some form. Colorlib: real numbers on only 5/30 HVAC and 5/19 electrician sites.

conversion_patterns.name: Manufacturer and dealer certifications
conversion_patterns.what: A row of manufacturer badges with the tier name and what it means for the customer: GAF Master Elite (GAF says fewer than 2% of roofers qualify; unlocks Golden Pledge warranty), Owens Corning Platinum Preferred, CertainTeed ShingleMaster; HVAC dealer status (Trane, Napoleon 'authorized dealer', Carrier, Lennox); Colorbond 'authorised installer'; hardscape (Keystone authorised); garage doors (LiftMaster, 'authorized Sommer dealer'); EV chargers (Tesla, Wallbox, Zappi).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 13/35 overall; roofing 7/7.
conversion_patterns.evidence: https://www.houstonroofingonline.com/ ; https://www.bonedry.com/ ; https://igniteheating.ca/ ; GAF blog via https://www.gaf.com/en-us/blog/your-home/2025-gaf-presidents-club-award-a-commitment-to-roofing-excellence-281474980403335

conversion_patterns.name: Trade-body and safety accreditations
conversion_patterns.what: Show the credential customers in that trade and country look for: pest = QualityPro, GreenPro, NPMA; painting = 'EPA Lead-Safe Certified' (RRP); UK = Gas Safe, NICEIC/NAPIT, NFRC, Which? Trusted Trader; AU = Master Plumbers / Master Electricians, CEC for solar; remodeling = NARI, NKBA; landscaping = NALP, ISA arborist number. Link each badge to its public register where one exists.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: About 15/35 (Arrow, Nozzle Nolen, Green Home, Hedlund, Catchlight, Pimlico, Aspect, BOXT, Fallon, Service Today, Carrington, Neil Kelly, Smock/ACCA, Bright/Worksafe, Bone Dry/NRCA).

conversion_patterns.name: A specific, named guarantee
conversion_patterns.what: Put a named guarantee near the CTA that states the remedy or the term: 'Happy You'll Be or the Service is Free' (Hiller); 'If something was missed, tell us right away. We'll come back and fix it for free.' (Tidy Casa); 'Always On-Time, Guaranteed' (Snell); '25-Year Craftsmanship Warranty' (Bone Dry); 'Backed by a 10-Year Warranty' (Hedlund); 1-year standard / 5-year heavy-duty (Garage Door Fix). A heading such as 'Satisfaction Guarantee' with no terms doesn't build trust.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 24/35 state a guarantee or warranty; 16/35 give a term or remedy; 7/35 show only a vague heading (Bright, DYAD, Powerful, Green Home, Lawn Lovers, Bumble, BOXT).

conversion_patterns.name: Real owner, crew and technician photos
conversion_patterns.what: Use real photos of the people who come to the house, in uniform, next to branded vans. Name the owner with a credential ('Owned and operated by licensed master plumber Jay Cunningham'; Garage Door Fix's 'husband-and-wife team'). An owner-promise block with a photo works well (Puetz). Larger firms show a team grid (Neil Kelly, about 60 headshots). Caption with first names; reviews often mention techs by name.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 10/35 show identifiable team or technician photos; 4/35 name the owner.

conversion_patterns.name: Captioned real job photos instead of stock
conversion_patterns.what: Show project photos captioned with the service and the town ('Clyde Hill', 'Queen Anne' cards at Hedlund), drone shots of finished roofs (Houston Roofing), crews on site (Puetz, Carrington). Don't use stock: AdobeStock filenames, generic 'tech-photo' and illustrated cleaners were all spotted. Every gallery item should say what was done and where.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: About 13/35 show identifiable real job imagery; at least 6/35 visibly use stock or illustrations (A1 Garage, Gutter and Roof Repairs, Aspect, Tidy Casa, Maid Marines, Powerful). Colorlib: gallery of work linked on 15/27 roofing and 12/23 painting sites.

conversion_patterns.name: Before/after pairs
conversion_patterns.what: Show paired before/after shots (slider or side by side), each labelled with the job and town. Strongest for painting, roof restoration, landscaping, cleaning, garage door replacement and remodeling. Keep 3-6 pairs on the homepage and the rest on service pages.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: Only 2/35 show before/after on the homepage (Gutter and Roof Repairs, Lawn Lovers); Chet's Roofing (reviewed) has two pairs. Colorlib: 6-7/23 painting sites. Many roundups name it as a top pattern, so it's an easy gap to fill.

conversion_patterns.name: Short quote form near the top
conversion_patterns.what: Put a form in or just below the hero with 3-5 fields: service (select), ZIP/postcode, name, phone (email and message optional). Use type=tel and autocomplete attributes. The button says what happens next ('Get My Free Estimate'). Show the reply-time promise and a 'Prefer to talk?' tel: link beside it. Never make 'How did you hear about us?' required. Colorlib's guidance: 'short enough to complete on a phone', 'a postcode and a phone number and nothing else', 'a quote form of four fields, in the hero'.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 17/35 have a form on the homepage; only about 5/35 put it in the first screen (Bone Dry, Houston Roofing, Pimlico, Aspect, Puetz). Field counts range from 2 (Aspect) to about 20 (Carrington), median about 6. Colorlib: form above the fold on 1/18 plumbing, 2/30 HVAC, 7/27 roofing, 1/19 electrician sites; electrician forms have a median of 5 fields.

conversion_patterns.name: Two-step form when you need detail
conversion_patterns.what: Step 1 asks for contact details, or service + ZIP. Step 2 asks for job detail, photos and a preferred time. A partial step 1 still gives you a lead. Arrow: contact + address, 'Continue', then service + message. Hook Agency highlights Beaver Roofing's multi-step quote form in the hero. Neil Kelly opens with a 2-select project finder.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 3/35 (Arrow, Neil Kelly, Aspect's 2-field start).

conversion_patterns.name: Real online booking with arrival windows
conversion_patterns.what: 'Book Online' must open a real scheduler (Housecall Pro, ServiceTitan, Jobber or similar) that shows arrival windows, not a contact form. Offer 'First Available', '8am - 12pm', '12pm - 4pm' (Service Today), or Morning/Afternoon plus weekdays (Nozzle Nolen, button 'Confirm Appointment'). Cleaning and lawn programs should allow full checkout ('Book online in 60 Seconds', Tidy Casa; 'ORDER NOW', Lawn Lovers).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: About 20/35 show a Book/Schedule CTA, but only about 6/35 lead to real self-serve booking (Aspect, Tidy Casa, Maid Marines, Powerful/Housecall Pro, BOXT, Service Today). Colorlib HVAC: 20/30 have a Book button, only 8 have a booking system behind it.

conversion_patterns.name: Text or chat as a third contact route
conversion_patterns.what: Offer 'Text Us' (Fallon has an SMS modal and a published text number) or a chat that a person answers (Garage Door Fix 'Chat with us!'; Powerful 'Chat With Us') for people who can't call from work. Load it lazily after interaction so it doesn't slow the page. Keep marketing SMS consent as a separate, unticked checkbox ('Consent is not a condition of purchase').
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 3/35; SMS-consent checkboxes appear on 7/17 observed forms.

conversion_patterns.name: Dated seasonal and audience offers
conversion_patterns.what: Run 1-2 offers tied to the season, each with an expiry date and short terms: '$99 Heating Tune-Up' (Hiller); 'Stay Cool Now. Pay Later!*' 'Offer ends 30 November 2026' (Fallon); first-service ('$35 off your first service', Arrow); audience ('$500 OFF FULL ROOF REPLACEMENT' for military, veterans, teachers, Bone Dry). Expire them automatically.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 15/35 run offers; only 5/35 show an expiry date (Guardian, Snell, BOXT, Fallon, Tidy Casa). Tidy Casa's had already expired.

conversion_patterns.name: Insurance claim help and storm-chaser differentiation (roofing)
conversion_patterns.what: A roofing section that explains the claim path: free inspection with a photo report, meeting the adjuster, documentation, what the homeowner pays (deductible). Pair it with a line that sets the company apart from storm chasers and points to its local office and years ('We're not a storm-chasing company that shows up, does the work, and disappears.' Houston; 'isn't just another storm-chaser' Tadlock). Never promise a 'free roof' or offer to waive deductibles.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 3/7 roofing sites (Bone Dry, Houston, Bumble). Colorlib: claim help on 7/27, storm/hail on 13/27. Hook Agency singles out Stormgrade for putting 'insurance claim help up front'.

conversion_patterns.name: Named maintenance or membership plan with perks
conversion_patterns.what: A named plan with listed perks and, ideally, a price: Smock Comfort Plan ('two tune-ups yearly, 15% off repairs, and $100 in Comfort Credits'); Fallon VIP ('No call-out fee'); Nozzle Nolen tiers 365 SELECT / Complete / Complete+ with 'Purchase Pest Control' online; recurring discounts ('weekly 20%, bi-weekly 15%, monthly 10%', Maid Marines); lawn programs (Carrington). Give it a hero CTA ('Explore Memberships', Smock).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: HVAC/heating 6/7; pest 3/3; landscaping 3/4; cleaning 1/2 publish recurring discounts. Colorlib HVAC: membership or maintenance plans on Sanborn's, Thelen, Kensington and others.

conversion_patterns.name: Stated fee policy (no surprise fees)
conversion_patterns.what: Emergency trades should state the fee rules: 'No emergency fees' (Snell); '$0 Emergency Fees' and no weekend surcharge (Garage Door Fix); 'Same Prices, 7 Days a Week' / 'No hidden costs or surcharges' (Pimlico); or disclose the call-out fee and say 'You approve the final price before any major work begins.' (Fallon).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 5/35 (Snell, Garage Door Fix, Pimlico, Fallon, Hiller 'NO FEE').

conversion_patterns.name: What happens next, in 3-6 steps
conversion_patterns.what: Number 3-6 steps from first contact to the finished job, and name the human in each (estimator, designer, superintendent): Hedlund 'On-site estimate' through 'Two-stage walkthrough QC'; Normandy 'a dedicated Project Superintendent'; Neil Kelly 5 steps ending 'Love Your Space, Guaranteed'; Puetz Reach out, Planning, We get to work; Carrington Discovery, Consultation, Estimate, Agreement.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 8/35 (Hedlund, Normandy, Neil Kelly, Puetz, Carrington, Anderson, Bumble, Gibbs).

conversion_patterns.name: Budget ranges or minimums for big projects
conversion_patterns.what: For high-ticket design/build work, publish a minimum or ask for a budget range so leads sort themselves: Gibbs 'minimum investment... starts at $12,000'; Carrington's investment dropdown '$3k-$5k' to '$60k-$100k+' with 'Prefer to discuss verbally'; Neil Kelly's kitchen and bath cost calculators.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 3/35 (Gibbs, Carrington, Neil Kelly).

conversion_patterns.name: Founding year and local ownership
conversion_patterns.what: Put the founding year and local/family ownership in the trust strip or hero subhead: 'Family Owned & Locally Operated' + 'Since 1989' (Bone Dry); 'Family Owned and Operated Since 1990' (Hiller); 'Trusted Since 1951' (Nozzle Nolen); 'locally owned for generations'. Use one founding year everywhere.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 28/35 state years in business; 13/35 state family or local ownership.

conversion_patterns.name: Who comes to the door: vetted employees
conversion_patterns.what: Say who will be in the customer's home: 'Every technician is a company employee, not a subcontractor' (Garage Door Fix); 'Background-checked' (Snell, Hiller, Tidy Casa); 'Bonded & Insured', 'Vetted' (Maid Marines); 'No Subcontractors' (Elegant Painting, Colorlib). Police and Working With Children checks in the opening paragraph (All Electrics AU, Zarla).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 5/35 (Garage Door Fix, Snell, Hiller, Tidy Casa, Maid Marines).

conversion_patterns.name: Pet and child safety statement
conversion_patterns.what: For treatments and products used inside or around the home, state safety in plain words and back it in the FAQ: 'child and pet safe products' (Green Home Pest); 'eco-friendly, pet-safe, and child-safe' (Maid Marines); 'safe for your kids, your pets' (SafeHaven).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: 2/5 pest+cleaning sites listed (plus SafeHaven, reviewed).

conversion_patterns.name: Hours and open-now status beside the phone
conversion_patterns.what: Show today's status and hours by the phone: 'Open Now' (Service Today), '7 Days 7AM TO 5PM' (Bright), 'Mon-Sun: 7am-8pm' (Houston Roofing). Painters and remodelers can list office hours and crew hours separately (Catchlight). They must match the Google Business Profile and schema.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: About 5/35.

conversion_patterns.name: FAQ that answers the money and risk questions
conversion_patterns.what: 6-10 FAQs on price, timing, insurance claims, safety, warranty and what's included, written to answer, not to stuff keywords. Green Home puts its '$49 per month' anchor in the FAQ; Bone Dry explains insurance claims and adjusters; Hedlund confirms 'Every estimate is free and provided in writing'; Garage Door Fix gives '$380-$480 + GST' for springs. Mark it up as FAQ content on the page only, not as self-serving review schema.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: About 8/35 have a substantive homepage FAQ.

conversion_patterns.name: Local schema and consistent name, address and phone (NAP)
conversion_patterns.what: Use one canonical name, address (or service area) and phone in the header, footer, contact page, JSON-LD and Google Business Profile. JSON-LD: the most specific LocalBusiness subtype (see schema_types), with name, url, telephone (E.164), address, geo, openingHoursSpecification, areaServed (City list), sameAs (GBP, Yelp, Facebook), and makesOffer/hasOfferCatalog of Service items. Don't add aggregateRating for your own reviews: Google makes self-serving LocalBusiness reviews ineligible for stars. Keep the name free of keywords (a GBP guideline).
conversion_patterns.prevalence: Phone/NAP mismatches on 5/35 (DYAD 923 vs 932; Neil Kelly, A1 Garage and Pimlico have different header/footer numbers; Hiller shares one number across locations). JSON-LD wasn't measured site by site; LocalBusiness schema was seen on TruTec and SafeHaven.

conversion_patterns.name: Service-area map and Google Maps link
conversion_patterns.what: A service-area map (static image or SVG with the town names) on the homepage or areas page, and a lazy-loaded Google Maps embed (click to load) on the contact page that links to the Business Profile. Don't load a Maps iframe above the fold on mobile because it hurts LCP. Service-area businesses that hide their address in GBP should map the area, not a home address.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: Not measurable from text extraction. Maps were referenced on Houston Roofing (service-area map), Bumble (office map) and Powerful Electrical (service map); Ritz Plumbing uses a hero map of review pins (Colorlib).

conversion_patterns.name: Fast mobile pages (Core Web Vitals)
conversion_patterns.what: Mobile targets at the 75th percentile: LCP of 2.5s or less, INP of 200ms or less, CLS of 0.1 or less. Hero image in AVIF/WebP with explicit width/height and preloaded. No autoplay hero video or slider above the fold. Defer chat, review and Maps widgets until interaction. Use system or self-hosted fonts with font-display: swap. Render content as static HTML, not client-side only, so search crawlers and AI assistants can read it.
conversion_patterns.prevalence: Not measured. Colorlib's audits show most trade sites run WordPress page builders (10 of 17 HVAC WordPress sites; 7 of 11 electrician WordPress sites), which tend to be heavy. 4 of about 45 sites fetched here returned little or no text to a non-JS reader.
conversion_patterns.evidence: https://web.dev/articles/vitals ; https://thinkwithgoogle.com/consumer-insights/consumer-trends/mobile-site-load-time-statistics/ (53% of mobile visits abandoned past 3s) ; https://colorlib.com/wp/hvac-company-website-examples/

typical_fields: 'How did you hear about us?' (5/17, often required)
trade-specific triage such as roof type (1/17, Gutter and Roof Repairs)
quote_form.observed_length: 2 fields (Aspect: service + postcode) to about 20 (Carrington); median about 6. Colorlib's electrician forms ran 4-8 fields, median 5.
quote_form.best_practice: Put a 4-field step 1 in or right under the hero: service (select), ZIP/postcode, name, mobile phone. Use type=tel, inputmode=numeric for ZIP, and autocomplete=name/tel/postal-code. Email and message are optional. The submit label says what happens: 'Get My Free Estimate' / 'Check availability' / 'Confirm Appointment'. Under the button, show the reply promise (e.g. 'We call back within 1 business hour, 7am-7pm') and a 'Prefer to talk? (xxx) xxx-xxxx' tel: link. An optional step 2 collects trade-specific details, photo upload and an arrival window, so a step-1-only submit is still a lead. Keep SMS marketing consent a separate, unticked, optional checkbox ('Consent is not a condition of purchase'). Never require 'How did you hear about us?'; ask it on the thank-you page. Thank-you state: confirm the next step, the time frame and the phone number. Long forms (Carrington about 20 fields; Medley 11 per Colorlib) and required full street address up front (Smock) are the main friction seen.

copy_patterns: Problem + time-frame headline: 'Garage Door Broken? We Fix It Today.' (Garage Door Fix); 'Need an Electrician in Charleston, SC Today?' (Powerful Electrical); 'Need a Trade Specialist? We Can Be There Today!*' (Fallon).
A benefit you can check, instead of a slogan: 'Your Roof Could Be Done Tomorrow' / 'Residential roofs installed in just one day.' (Tadlock); 'Get a fixed price in minutes.' (BOXT).

Trade + place in the H1 for relevance: 'Heating & Cooling Services in Frederick & Montgomery County' (Smock); 'Seattle-Area Painters You Can Trust' (Hedlund); 'Same Day Pest Control Services in Southeast FL' (Nozzle Nolen).

Lead with the guarantee: '200% Guaranteed Home Cleaning' (Tidy Casa); 'Happy You'll Be or the Service is Free' (Hiller); 'The Best Techs. The Best Service. 100% Guaranteed.' (Hiller); badge 'Backed by a 10-Year Warranty' (Hedlund).

Name the fear and answer it in the subhead: 'a free written estimate with no surprise change orders' (Hedlund); 'shows you what your roof actually needs, then does the work right.' (Houston Roofing); 'Straight talk on budget, timing, and risk.' (Neil Kelly); 'No bait-and-switch. No pressure.' (A1 Garage).
Plain-spoken honesty positioning: 'Plumbing repairs. Real people. Honest answers.' (Superior Plumbing); 'THE EASIEST WAY TO REMODEL, HONESTLY.' (Neil Kelly).
Promises in a dot-separated row under the hero: 'Same-day repair · Published prices · No emergency fees' (Garage Door Fix).

Speed and effort microcopy on booking CTAs: 'Book online in 60 Seconds.' (Tidy Casa); 'Takes 60 seconds • No credit card required.' (Maid Marines); 'Book online in under a minute!' (Service Today); 'Online quote in under 1 minute' (BOXT).
Soft secondary call CTA: 'Prefer to talk? (732) 536-6500' (Arrow); 'or call us on 1300 743 923' (DYAD); 'need a tree removal? Call (503) 659-3172' (Anderson).
Availability that says who answers: 'answered 24/7 by a real person' (Powerful); '24/7 Live Answering Service' (Smock); '24/7 availability on nights, weekends, and holidays at no extra cost' (Snell).

Cut-off rules instead of vague 'fast service': 'If you book before midday, we guarantee a technician will be at your door that same day.' (Service Today); 'Available when you call before noon' (Nozzle Nolen); 'most appointments set within 24 hours' (Tadlock).

First-person CTA labels that name the free thing: 'Get My Free Estimate' (Tadlock); 'Schedule My Pest Service Now' (SafeHaven); 'Get Your Instant Price' (Maid Marines); 'Start My Project' (Neil Kelly).
Button text that says what happens next: 'Check availability' (Aspect); 'Confirm Appointment' (Nozzle Nolen); 'Send Booking Request' (Pimlico).
Form opener in the customer's words: 'I need help with...' (Pimlico); 'Tell us about your project' (Catchlight); 'Let Our Team Earn Your Trust' (Bone Dry).
Monthly-payment framing for big tickets: 'New HVAC System for as little as $113/month' (Snell); 'Split Systems Installed from just $14.75/week' (Fallon); 'BUY NOW, PAY LATER' (Tadlock).
Separate yourself from storm chasers: 'We're not a storm-chasing company that shows up, does the work, and disappears.' (Houston Roofing); 'isn't just another storm-chaser.' (Tadlock).
Proof stats from operations, not adjectives: 'Same-day service on 95% of calls' (Garage Door Fix); '85%' first-time fix rate, '230+' tradespeople (Pimlico); '12,104' Google reviews (Bone Dry).
Local-pride or memorable line: 'Pimlico Plumbers. Built for London.'; 'From the Furnace to the Faucet, Snell's Got It' (Snell); vanity number '844-MYHILLER' (Hiller).
Reassure on fees: 'Same Prices, 7 Days a Week' / 'No hidden costs or surcharges' (Pimlico); 'You approve the final price before any major work begins.' (Fallon); 'No emergency fees' (Snell).
Who-shows-up line: 'Every technician is a company employee, not a subcontractor' (Garage Door Fix); 'background-checked cleaners with all supplies included' (Tidy Casa).
anti_patterns: No printed phone number in the header (icon only, footer only, or missing): Bumble Roofing, Aspect (icon only), BOXT, Neil Kelly, plus reviewed Phinney Ridge Painting, RYAN Lawn & Tree and di Stefano Landscaping. Colorlib: 6/19 electrician sites have no tappable number at all.

Phone printed as text but not a tel: link: Mango Landscapes (UK); Colorlib flags Circle Plumbing ('Phone number in headline but not tappable'), Kleinberg, JTM and O'Connell Electric, and 3/30 HVAC sites.

Different phone numbers on the same page (header vs footer vs sticky bar), which breaks NAP consistency and confuses callers: DYAD (1300 743 923 vs 932), Neil Kelly, A1 Garage, Pimlico; Hiller shows one number for two different locations.

'Book Online' / 'Schedule' buttons that lead to a generic contact form or nowhere: Guardian ('Book Online' to the contact page), Superior Plumbing, The Irish Plumber, A1 Garage (one button links to '#'). Colorlib: 12/30 HVAC sites show a booking button with no booking system behind it.

Ratings with no count or source ('5.0/5.0 Rated', Bright Electrical), or a review widget with a missing number ('With over [blank] positive reviews', Service Today). BrightLocal 2026: 47% won't use a business with under 20 reviews, so the count matters.

The same figure differs within one page: review counts (Smock 1,500+ vs 1,899; Puetz 363+ vs 375; Anderson 300+ vs 100+), years (Gutter and Roof Repairs 30+ vs 20+; Fallon '60yrs' vs '10 Years'; SafeHaven 70 years vs almost a century vs 1955), checklist points (Maid Marines 85 vs 100), prices (BOXT £1,890 vs £1,745).

Placeholder or broken content shipped live: 'Lorem ipsum' testimonial (The Irish Plumber); 'Need some text here.' in a modal (Nozzle Nolen); '0+ Years of Combined Experience' counter (Guardian); 'No Project Found' sections and a calculator with no inputs (Best Bet Lawn); an unlabeled 'New Field' (Superior Plumbing); four service buttons on one bit.ly link (Powerful Electrical).
Claims the footer contradicts: '24/7' next to 'Business hours are Mon-Fri 8am-4pm' (Powerful Electrical); '24/7 Answering Service' next to 'Closed: Sunday' (Guardian).
Stale or expired offers: Tidy Casa still advertised an October promo code in November; page copyright '© 2023' (Phinney Ridge). An expired coupon suggests nobody is maintaining the site.

An asterisk with no terms, and superlatives with no backing: 'Same day service or it's FREE!*' (Service Today); 'UK's most trusted*' with no footnote (BOXT); 'the undisputed industry leader' (A1 Garage); '#1 Best Licensed Electrician' in alt text (Powerful).

Vague guarantee headings with no terms: 'Satisfaction Guarantee' (Bright), 'Workmanship Guarantee' (DYAD), 'Treatment Guarantees' (SafeHaven), 'Exceptional Quality Guaranteed' (Lawn Lovers). 7/35 do this.

'Licensed & insured' with no licence number, even where the number is legally required in ads (California CSLB, Queensland QBCC): 23/35 studied sites print no licence number; Colorlib finds real numbers on only 5/30 HVAC and 5/19 electrician sites.

Stock or illustrated people instead of the real crew: AdobeStock filenames (Gutter and Roof Repairs), stock-style 'tech-photo' (A1 Garage), illustrated team (Maid Marines), generic action shots (Tidy Casa, Aspect).

Long forms with required low-value fields: Carrington (about 20 fields), Houston Roofing (6 required incl. 'How Did You Hear About Us?'), Green Home (5 of 6 required), Smock (full street address required). Colorlib: Medley HVAC's 11-field form.
No quote form near the top: only about 5/35 put a form in the first screen; Colorlib finds forms above the fold on just 1/18 plumbing, 2/30 HVAC and 1/19 electrician sites.

Generic or brand-name hero headlines that say nothing about the job or place: 'Ignite Heating and Air Conditioning.' (Ignite), 'Creativity. Quality. Experience.' (Gibbs), 'Beautiful, Lasting Results' (Catchlight), 'Professional Roofing Services Across the U.S.' (Bumble).

Service area hidden or vague ('Servicing Perth', 'North Brisbane', or none): Bright, DYAD, Gibbs; area lists that differ between body and footer (Tidy Casa, Hiller, Garage Door Fix); H1 city vs H2 cities mismatch (TruTec).

Looks great but is hard to contact: Colorlib's top plumbing pick (Parklane Plumbing) has 'No clickable phone in the opening screen, no licence claim, no homepage quote form'; di Stefano Landscaping has no header phone and no hero CTA.

Navigation cards that all link to the same page (Bright Electrical's Commercial, EV Chargers and Energy Solutions cards all go to the residential page), which wastes service-page SEO and confuses visitors.
Operational problems announced on the homepage: Superior Plumbing repeats 'WE ARE CURRENTLY EXPERIENCING SOME PHONE ISSUES' four times; fix the phones and route calls before advertising.

Content that only renders with JavaScript: several sites (e.g. Sharper Impressions Painting, Nova Landscape & Design, JT Madison Landscaping) returned little or no text to a non-JS fetch. Crawlers and AI assistants may see an empty page, which matters now that 45% of consumers use AI tools for local recommendations (BrightLocal 2026).
schema_notes: schema.org subtypes of HomeAndConstructionBusiness are exactly: Electrician, GeneralContractor, HVACBusiness, HousePainter, Locksmith, MovingCompany, Plumber, RoofingContractor. Landscaping, pest control, cleaning and garage doors have no dedicated type, so use HomeAndConstructionBusiness ('provides services around homes and buildings') and describe the trade with makesOffer -> Offer -> itemOffered Service {serviceType: 'Pest control'}.

Google: 'Use the most specific LocalBusiness sub-type possible'. Multi-trade businesses can give an array, e.g. ["Plumber", "HVACBusiness", "Electrician"]. Google does not support additionalType for this feature.

Required by Google: name and address (PostalAddress). Recommended: telephone (with country code), url, geo (5+ decimals), openingHoursSpecification (24/7 = all 7 days, opens 00:00, closes 23:59), priceRange (under 100 characters). Add areaServed (City/AdministrativeArea list matching the on-page list) and sameAs (GBP, Yelp, Facebook, BBB).

Don't add aggregateRating or review markup for reviews of your own business: Google makes self-serving LocalBusiness/Organization reviews ineligible for star rich results, including those from embedded third-party widgets.

Service-area businesses: Google says to hide the street address in the Business Profile when customers aren't served there, and to keep service areas within about 2 hours' drive of the base. Keep the site's NAP identical to the Business Profile and use a local number rather than a central call-centre number.
